Huainan and Hefei circles stand for the country south of the Huai. Sun Ce's Jiangdong conquests 194 to early 197 were made 'for him' and are shown as a vassal tie (ledger), not drawn here.

ledger.note: 189: Yuan Shu holds Nanyang. Infobox: 'Administrator of Nanyang 189-192'; he took the commandery after Sun Jian killed its grand administrator Zhang Zi (no month).
192: Nanyang is left. The infobox ends his Nanyang office in 192 and the page says he 'first held Nanyang, then moved to Chenliu'; PAGE SILENT on who held Nanyang next.
192: Chenliu. He 'moved to Chenliu and extended his influence into Yang Province in 192'.
193: Chenliu is lost. His 193 defeat at Fengqiu came from 'the combined armies of Cao Cao and Yuan Shao'; 'After defeats in early 193, he fled to Shouchun'.

ledger.note: 193: Shouchun and the Huai country. He fled to Shouchun, deposed Inspector Chen Wen of Yang Province and took that title (self-appointed Governor of Yang Province 192-197); the End of the Han page: he 'controlled the area south of the Huai River'.
195: Sun Ce conquers Jiangdong 'for him'. 'Sun Ce and Wu Jing conquered many Jiangdong territories for him from 194 to early 197' (194 on the page; sun-ce's dossier dates the crossing to 195).

197: Yuan Shu proclaims himself emperor. He 'proclaimed himself emperor in early 197, under the short-lived Zhong dynasty' (footnote: the first three months of Jian'an 2, 5 February to 4 May 197), citing the Imperial Seal given him by Sun Jian; the End of the Han page: he 'declared himself Son of Heaven' at Shouchun. Same state, governor to emperor.
197: Sun Ce defects. 'Sun Ce defected, which the article calls 'Most devastating of the departures and defections'' (no month); the conquests ran 'from 194 to early 197'.

notes:
Yuan Shu, Nanyang then the Huai country, 189-199. 2 pages opened (Yuan Shu, End of the Han dynasty); no Cliopatria row. Unsettled: (1) the page gives no borders ('built up a powerful warlord state'), the Huainan and Hefei circles are a stand-in; (2) who held Nanyang after 192 and Shouchun after 199 (nobody entered, confidence 1); (3) 194 (Yuan Shu page) against 195 (sun-ce dossier) for Sun Ce's crossing: the vassal tie is entered at 195; (4) the page says the Zhong dynasty was proclaimed at Shouchun (End of the Han page), not on the Yuan Shu page; (5) Lujiang and Liu Xun.
Counterparts: han-dynasty, cao-cao exist; sun-ce and yuan-shao are written by this batch; lu-bu and liu-bei have no dossier (lu-bu held Xu Province 196-198: a candidate).
